issues.rule_name: NULL Values Detected in User Email Column

_full_remediation.sql_fix:
-- Fix NULL values in users.email
-- Step 1: Count NULLs
SELECT COUNT(*) as null_count
FROM users
WHERE email IS NULL;

-- Step 2: Update with default value
UPDATE users
SET email = 'DEFAULT_VALUE'  -- Replace with appropriate default
WHERE email IS NULL;

-- Step 3: Add NOT NULL constraint (optional)
ALTER TABLE users
MODIFY COLUMN email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL;
manual_steps: 1. Review business rules for 'email' default values
2. Check upstream data source for root cause of NULLs
3. Execute SQL update with appropriate default value
4. Add NOT NULL constraint if column is required
5. Implement validation at data ingestion layer
_full_remediation.impact_analysis: NULL values in 'email' cause application errors. Immediate fix recommended.
_full_remediation.prevention_strategy: Add NOT NULL constraint and implement default value logic in ETL

_full_remediation.sql_fix:
-- Remove duplicates
-- Step 1: Identify duplicates
SELECT unique_column, COUNT(*) as count
FROM customers
GROUP BY unique_column
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

-- Step 2: Delete duplicates (keep first occurrence)
DELETE FROM customers
WHERE id NOT IN (
  SELECT MIN(id)
  FROM customers
  GROUP BY unique_column
);

-- Step 3: Add UNIQUE constraint
ALTER TABLE customers
ADD CONSTRAINT unique_constraint UNIQUE (unique_column);
